report_title: Breaking agent backbones: Evaluating the security of backbone LLMs in AI agents
models: 31 popular backbone LLMs powering AI agents (b³ benchmark, 194,331 crowdsourced adversaria
finding: Introduces 'threat snapshots' and the b³ benchmark (194,331 crowdsourced adversarial attacks) to isolate security-critical execution points in AI agents, then evaluates 31 backbone LLMs. Enhanced reasoning capability improved backbone security, whereas model size did not correlate with security. report_title: "Did you lie?": Evaluating Lie Detectors across Model Scale and Belief-Verified
models: 31 open-weight models (2B-1T parameters) plus custom-built reasoning 'model organisms'; fo
finding: Evaluating lie detectors across 31 open-weight models: on prompted lying all four detectors scale positively with model capability, but every activation/logprob detector degrades sharply against belief-verified trained 'model organisms' (DYL retains most signal). Conclusion: current lie detectors cannot support high-confidence claims about model beliefs.

report_title: Lessons from studying two-hop latent reasoning
finding: In controlled tests, LLMs fail to compose two purely synthetic facts but succeed at latent two-hop (compositional) reasoning when one fact is synthetic and one is natural, demonstrating genuine latent internal reasoning while leaving open how the ability scales with model size. Relevant to the limits of chain-of-thought monitoring.
